node.title: Re^5: Blessing with unknown classnames
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I mean this: if (defined $err) can become if (defined($err) && ($err eq 'YouveGotError')), so that it errors only on'YouveGotError' blessed refs and nothing else, because the sub may normally return other blessed things.

I'm not sure if this is a question, but just in case, note that I fully agree with [kcott] that [doc://Scalar::Util]'s blessed (a core module) is the "correct" answer to the question of how to tell if a [doc://ref]erence is [doc://bless]ed or not. But if the sub also can return other blessed refs, and you want to differentiate them, then one possible solution is what you said in your root node: creating an "error" class is one way. But since Perl's OO system is so nice and simple, inheritance can be incredibly simple, as I show in the following example. Of course, there are existing solutions on CPAN, e.g. [mod://Throwable] and [mod://Exception::Class].

use warnings; use strict; use Scalar::Util qw/blessed/; @Error::ISA = qw//; # "base class" for errors @BadInput::ISA = qw/Error/; sub doit { my $in = shift; if ( $in =~ /foo/ ) { return bless [123,456], 'RealReturnValue'; } else { return bless ['abc','def'], 'BadInput'; } } for my $val ("foobar", "quzbaz") { my $ret = doit($val); if ( my $err = blessed $ret and $ret->isa('Error') ) { print "$val -> Error: $err\n"; } else { print "$val -> OK\n"; } } __END__ foobar -> OK quzbaz -> Error: BadInput
